chunks: 3583 - It is narrated from Sadīr al-Ṣayrafī, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “A report has reached me about al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and if it is true, then—”
“Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return.”

He said: “And what is it?” I said: “It has reached me that al-Ḥasan used to say: ‘If his brain were to boil from the heat of the sun, he would not seek shade by the wall of a moneychanger; and if his liver were to burst forth for water, while that is my work and my trade, and upon it my flesh and blood have grown, and from it are my hajj and my ʿumrah.’”

He said: Then he sat upright, عليه السلام, and then said: “Al-Ḥasan has lied. Take fairly and give fairly. When the salat arrives, then leave what is in your hand and rise for the salat. Did you not know that the Companions of the Cave were moneychangers?”

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ: the Companions of the Cave, cited here as an example connected to this profession
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the prescribed salat (prayer) whose time takes priority over work
key_terms.الصَّيْرَفِيِّ: a moneychanger; one engaged in exchanging currency
key_terms.حَجَّتِي: my hajj, performed from lawful earnings
key_terms.سَوَاءً: with fairness and equality in taking and giving
key_terms.عُمْرَتِي: my ʿumrah, performed from lawful earnings

ai.seo_question: Is working as a moneychanger or engaging in trade permissible in Islam if done fairly?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the disparagement of lawful trade, specifically moneychanging, when conducted with fairness and justice. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام affirms that honest economic activity is permissible, while emphasizing that one must leave worldly work when the time of salat arrives.
